question: Does a standards-derived bounded causal autoregressive Gaussian source, fit label-blind on the frozen P4R development scans, improve both NPS and ACF on sealed confirmation scans over the retained single anisotropic Gaussian-kernel P4T baseline?

research_basis.scope: Clean-room spatial-source baseline using the current standard's explicit causal AR family. This is not a wire-compatible AFGS1 implementation and does not copy reference code.

split.normalization_and_fit: Each fixed development crop/channel is quadratically detrended in scanner-code divided by its crop mean, standardized to unit variance, and contributes equal normal-equation weight.

model.neighbor_pattern: For lag L: all offsets (dy,dx) with dy=-L..-1 and dx=-L..L, plus current-row offsets (0,-L)..(0,-1); count=2*L*(L+1).
model.selection: Minimize the maximum of development median NPS-error ratio and median ACF-error ratio versus P4T, then their sum, then lag.

branch_rule.pass: Retain one generic standards-derived AR spatial-source candidate and open a separately frozen P4AQ positive density/transmittance integration plus fit-forbidden P4Z external confirmation.
branch_rule.fail: Close this bounded AR representation without coefficient, lag, split, metric or threshold rescue; retain P4AF as the full-resolution synthetic reference and P4T only as prior generic scanner-convolved development evidence.

forbidden_fallbacks: read confirmation pixels before all coefficients, lag selection and normalization are frozen
fit per-channel, per-stock, per-scan or per-image coefficients
clip fitted coefficients into the allowed range
retune lag, ridge, coefficient step, split, seeds, metrics or thresholds after confirmation
call scanner-code AR parameters physical emulsion grain, stock response or scanner-independent
photographic rendering or product integration in this leaf
claim_ceiling: Development/confirmation evidence for one generic standards-derived scanner-convolved AR spatial-source baseline; not AFGS1 wire conformance, physical emulsion geometry, stock/process/scanner calibration, photographic quality or product promotion.
